comparison: Both evaluations support the methanol fixation findings (C1, C14-C18). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on quantitative data and statistical significance. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED, calling it 'a major result' and 'significant,' confirming the manuscript addresses the negative control request (C18). Strong agreement on this core finding.

Significant disagreement on F-actin stabilizer experiments (C20-C24). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, emphasizing strong quantitative evidence and convergence of multiple approaches. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, expressing concern that phalloidin/jasplakinolide may create artifacts by 'perturbing an equilibrium' rather than revealing physiological conditions. Reviewers question whether results reflect true biology.

Disagreement on spatial heterogeneity claims (C2, C25-C26). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED but notes lack of quantification limits strength. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN and explicitly request quantification: 'This difference should be quantified.' Both identify the same weakness but peer reviewers are more critical about the insufficient support.

Disagreement on siRNA knockdown evidence (C3, C30-C31, C38). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED despite acknowledging Western blot/qRT-PCR limitations. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, stating 'There is no good evidence in the literature that the siRNA technique used works' and requesting validation and quantification of knockdown. Peer reviewers more skeptical of the methodology.

Perfect agreement on γ-actin distribution and antibody specificity (C27-C29, C40-C42). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes differential staining patterns ruling out cross-reactivity. Peer reviewers confirm the manuscript satisfactorily addressed their concern about potential antibody cross-reactivity with γ-actin. Strong concordance.

Strong agreement on the central conclusion (C4, C32-C34, C39). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes convergence of multiple experimental approaches. Peer reviewers state the manuscript 'demonstrate[s] conclusively' that pericytes contain α-SMA and 'resolves an ongoing controversy.' Minor editorial requests for percentage data do not diminish overall support.

Disagreement on transgenic mouse explanations (C35-C36). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, calling these 'post-hoc explanations without direct experimental validation' that remain 'plausible but hypothetical.' Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED and did not challenge these interpretations. Peer reviewers more accepting of speculative explanations.

Both address vessel order and oxygen delivery context (C37 in OpenEval; C37, C43-C47 in peer review). OpenEval rates C37 as SUPPORTED but notes correlation is not mechanistic. Peer reviewers rate broader contextual claims as SUPPORTED without challenge. General agreement on appropriateness of contextualization.

Agreement on neurovascular coupling context (C43-C47). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes claims are 'well-supported by multiple citations' and appropriately contextualize findings. Peer reviewers did not challenge these literature-based contextual claims. Strong concordance on background framing.

Perfect agreement on historical context and controversy (C48-C50). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these 'accurately summarize prior work' and provide important context. Peer reviewers did not challenge these literature summaries. Strong concordance on background claims.

Disagreement on significance and impact claims (C51-C52). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, calling these 'speculative statements about potential future impact' that are 'reasonable hypotheses for future work but not supported conclusions.' Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, affirming the findings 'represent an important advance' and 'resolve an ongoing controversy.' Peer reviewers more accepting of broader significance claims.

Perfect agreement on background literature (C5-C12). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes claims 'accurately summarize the historical context and prior literature through appropriate citations.' Peer reviewers did not challenge these literature summaries. Strong concordance on establishing scientific context.

Perfect agreement on methodological details (C53-C54). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these are 'straightforward methodological details that are appropriately documented.' Peer reviewers did not question these details. Strong concordance on basic methods reporting.

Partial overlap on pericyte identification and F-actin detection (C13, C19). OpenEval includes these claims in broader methanol fixation evaluation (R1, SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers separately evaluate pericyte markers as SUPPORTED without concerns. Both agree on adequacy of pericyte identification methods.
